wrong_assumption: Qatar's drinking water comes mostly from groundwater.
correction: Drinking water is desalinated. Desalination supplied 63% of all water produced in 2023, with groundwater going mostly to farms.

wrong_assumption: Abstraction fell in 2023, so pumping went down.
correction: Kahramaa revised its estimate from 250 to 200 million m3 using modelling. The change is in the estimate, not proven pumping.
They are estimates. Kahramaa says flowmeters will be installed in every well within three years.
3-5 times matches the 2019-2022 estimate and QEERI 2022. With 2023 official figures it is about 2.7 times recharge and 4 times safe yield.

wrong_assumption: Recharge and safe yield are the same thing.
correction: Safe yield is recharge minus natural outflow: 74.7 - 25.1 = 49.6 million m3 a year.

wrong_assumption: Low TDS means the water is safe to drink.
correction: WHO sets no health-based value for TDS. Safety needs microbiological and chemical tests.

wrong_assumption: A TDS sensor reading can show groundwater is drinkable.
correction: The SEN0244 probe reads up to 1,000 ppm, while the 2020 well survey averaged several thousand mg/L, and TDS alone never shows safety.
Brackish water can still irrigate salt-tolerant crops with management, under FAO 29's restriction levels.
